lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When the buttons start at twenty, twenty starts to feel like the *cheap* choice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then comes a second push: someone is standing right there, *watching* you choose.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a coffee shop experiment, the tip screen mostly made people feel *worse* about the shop.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A study of thirteen million New York taxi rides found higher buttons raised tips about ten *percent*.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But with those higher buttons, more riders gave up and left *no* tip at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So decide your tip before you reach the counter, and press *custom* if the buttons are not yours.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every screen asks now because higher buttons really do make people tip *more*.
